The route at main.py:307-324 supplies the authenticated organisation, never a request-supplied tenant. test_sessions.py:210-224 specifies session success and bearer rejection; tests were read, not executed.

local_checks.result: payment_evidence first selects PaymentIntent by organisation_id and globally unique public_id. Operations, attempts, histories, events, recipients, deliveries, delivery attempts, financial resources, journals, postings, idempotency records and endpoint-version identifiers each retain an organisation predicate plus selected-parent identifiers. The ledger-account join also matches organisation. Responses explicitly select metadata, hashes and financial fields rather than secret ciphertext or raw request/response bytes. No cross-tenant path or narrower session environment authority was established.

local_checks.invariant: Repeated login attempts under one limiter key must not accumulate unlimited timestamps.
local_checks.result: main.py:120 configures ten events per 60 seconds. rate_limit.py:26-48 serializes checks, removes expired timestamps, rejects before appending an eleventh active timestamp, and therefore bounds each deque at ten. Login calls the limiter before opening the authentication transaction (main.py:333-335); later authentication failure does not undo accounting. The existing retry/expiry test covers this behavior, but was not executed.

local_checks.invariant: Distinct login keys should have bounded retention and cleanup without establishing unsupported shared availability impact.
local_checks.result: rate_limit.py:27-37 uses 10,000 as a cleanup trigger, not an admission cap: it scans the map, deletes half the fully expired keys, then admits a new key even when none expired. Cleanup is request-driven; idle state remains until subsequent checks or process termination. Existing test_rate_limit.py:20-35 exercises only expired-key cleanup, not active-key saturation. Active cardinality can exceed the trigger and scans cost O(N) under the shared lock, but no bounded input causing meaningful cross-user resource impact was established independently of key-admission assumptions. This remains hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Cardinality conclusions must distinguish source-visible ingress and process scope from assumed attacker control of effective client identities.
local_checks.result: main.py:329-333 selects the first forwarded value or client host; the console forwards that header. Caddy routes /api/* to the API; the production overlay removes direct API host ports. edge/origin.py:103 guards selected prefixes excluding session login. asgi.py creates one app with process-local limiter state, consistent with README.md:275. These sources do not establish deployed effective forwarded-header normalization or attacker access to arbitrarily many effective client identities. No Caddy default or deployed routing behavior was assumed, and the peer-owned XFF trust hypothesis was not reported.

hardening_notes: packages/relaypay/identity/rate_limit.py:27-37: enforce an actual aggregate admission bound and avoid scanning every tracked key on every check above the cleanup threshold. Add deterministic source-level regression cases for all-active keys at capacity, exactly one expired key, and repeated cleanup. The current missing hard cap alone does not establish a security finding.

local_checks.invariant: An unauthenticated scrape must not impose disproportionate database work on the shared API pool.
local_checks.result: When enabled, each unauthenticated GET /metrics opens a transaction on the API engine, performs six database-wide counts and enumerates all connectors before rendering metrics. No per-scrape cache or application rate gate is visible. The transaction closes after refresh; source alone does not establish actual contention or query cost.

local_checks.invariant: Determine whether configuration and ingress controls prevent a lower-trust requester from reaching the scrape handler.
local_checks.result: Observability defaults off. The development compose exposes the API port; the production overlay removes that mapping. Actual deployment routing, enablement and upstream limits are not established by source.

excluded_blocks.reason: The only source readers of request_logs are the usage and operational-metrics allowlist entries (operations/service.py:101-110), which the organisation-scoped units 28, 30 and 31 cover; no source reader of usage_rollups exists in apps or packages.

local_checks.invariant: Local mirror of apps/api/main.py:167-227 with the unmodified record_request, retention 3 and forced prune: unmatched raw path keys, template keys for matched routes, 256-char and 12-char truncation, method tokens, edge-rejected (401) keying, request_logs bound versus usage_rollups growth, tenant-scope eviction, and duplicate X-Request-ID behaviour
local_checks.result: Promoted run exit 0. Six unmatched GET paths returned 404 and created six distinct usage_rollups rows keyed by raw path. Matched evidence GET (two IDs) and POST (405) were keyed by the template /api/v1/payment_intents/{payment_id}/evidence. A 300-char path was stored as 256 chars. Method tokens were stored truncated (ZZTOKEN-ALPH, X0-PROBE, X1-PROBE) as separate rows. An edge-rejected 401 request with no edge headers created a raw-path rollup row. With retention 3 and prune probability 1.0, request_logs stayed at 3 while usage_rollups grew from 3 to 8 with no deletion. Three anonymous writes evicted a tenant request_log row while the tenant rollup survived. The duplicate X-Request-ID result is invalid: the driver sent a mixed-case header name, so Starlette generated fresh IDs and no duplicate was exercised. Driver mirrors the middleware and does not import create_app.

local_checks.invariant: Route key fallback for unmatched requests in the request-metadata middleware: request.url.path and request.method reach record_request unvalidated
local_checks.result: apps/api/main.py:181 sets route to the matched template only when scope route is set, otherwise to raw request.url.path. Lines 184-185 pass request.method unvalidated. Line 214 calls record_request for every non-health request, with organisation_id None for anonymous callers (line 217) and raw route and method (lines 219-220). No flag gates the write; OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED gates only /metrics (line 298).

local_checks.invariant: Middleware ordering: edge HMAC rejection versus metadata write
local_checks.result: install_edge_origin_boundary is called at main.py:122, before the security_headers decorator at main.py:167. Starlette wraps later-added HTTP middleware outermost, so security_headers wraps edge_origin_boundary (origin.py:98-122). A 401 from the edge check still reaches record_request. Confirmed locally by the C_D check.

local_checks.invariant: usage_rollups lifecycle: any delete, prune, cap or retention for rollup rows
local_checks.result: service.py:59 writes route[:256] and service.py:58 method[:12] unchanged into the upsert key (on conflict at service.py:66-72 over bucket_start, scope_key, method, route, status_class). The only DELETE in the module is the RequestLog prune at service.py:86-92. A repository-wide search finds no DELETE, prune or cleanup of usage_rollups in apps, packages, scripts or migrations, other than test cleanup in tests/integration/test_m7_observability.py. models.py:44-45 describes rollups as low-cardinality, and models.py:65 stores route as String(256) with no key cap. 0018:22 classifies usage_rollups as C (mutable, no trigger); 0012:47-81 creates it with no retention.

local_checks.invariant: Documented contract (bounded route templates and low-cardinality rollups) versus implementation
local_checks.result: observability.md:7 states histograms use bounded route templates rather than raw paths; observability.md:8-10 says request logs store a route template and REQUEST_LOG_RETENTION bounds raw metadata rows while hourly rollups remain durable. configuration.md:88 describes REQUEST_LOG_RETENTION as an approximate cap on raw request-log rows only. config.py:81 defines the default 10000. The implementation stores raw unmatched paths in usage_rollups, which violates the template contract. No document accepts unbounded rollup growth.

local_checks.invariant: Readers of request_logs and usage_rollups are organisation-scoped and do not expose anonymous rows
local_checks.result: operations/service.py:101-110 maps the usage and operational-metrics resources to request_logs only. list_operations_resource filters by organisationId and environmentId (lines 195-197), and _environment_scope (lines 141-155) requires the principal organisation. No reader of usage_rollups exists in apps or packages. Anonymous rows are therefore not returned to any tenant reader in source.

local_checks.invariant: Ingress bounds on which unmatched paths reach the origin and whether unauthenticated volume is limited
local_checks.result: Caddyfile:8-9 forwards every /api/* and /health/* path to api:8000, with no rate limit, path allowlist or body limit in this file. Caddyfile:14 sends other paths to the console. index.ts:135 forwards every /api/v1/* path to the origin, and index.ts:136 returns 404 for other paths. Unmatched /api/v1/* paths therefore reach record_request through the Worker, and any /api/* path through Caddy. No source-visible per-path or per-client limit applies.

local_checks.invariant: Synchronous DB commit inside an async HTTP middleware on every non-health request
local_checks.result: security_headers (main.py:168) is async and calls the synchronous record_request (main.py:214; service.py:25-43), which runs a blocking SQLAlchemy commit on the event loop for every non-health request, including unauthenticated 404s, with no per-source limit before it. database.py:19-27 sets pool_pre_ping but no pool size or timeout. Volume-driven availability effect; not validated because stress testing is excluded.

local_checks.invariant: Client X-Request-ID as a unique metadata key and exception handling in the middleware
local_checks.result: request_logs.request_id is unique (models.py:35). The client header is used unvalidated (main.py:169) and truncated to 96 chars (service.py:46). A duplicate raises IntegrityError inside the transaction, which also rolls back the rollup increment. main.py:225-226 logs and swallows the exception. This was not exercised locally: the driver's header-name case was wrong, so the duplicate was never sent. Source-derived only.

unresolved: Deployed ingress filtering (Cloudflare Worker routing beyond /api/v1/*, any CDN or WAF in front of Caddy) is not source-visible. It can only reduce the reachable key count. Owner check: distinct anonymous route keys per hour at the origin in staging.
Whether the origin server accepts non-standard HTTP method tokens is not established from source; the method dimension depends on it.
No out-of-repo retention or cleanup job for usage_rollups is established. Owner check: row count of usage_rollups where scope_key is anonymous:none after one retention window.
discovery_reason: Every non-health request, including unauthenticated and unmatched ones, reaches record_request (apps/api/main.py:211-225). For unmatched routes the route label is the raw request path (main.py:180-181), truncated to 256 characters (observability/service.py:50, 59). Each distinct label creates a new usage_rollups row per hour and scope (service.py:55-85; models.py:44-45 describes the table as low-cardinality). No code deletes usage_rollups: the only prune is the 1 percent RequestLog delete (service.py:86-92), and migration 0018 classifies usage_rollups as class C with no immutability trigger (0018_immutability_backfill.py:22). The retention bound therefore covers request_logs only, while rollup growth from anonymous unique paths is unbounded. The prune itself sorts the whole log via offset (service.py:88-90). No ledger unit references usage_rollups or record_request.

format_retry_note: Two prior hunter results wrapped JSON in prose; not accepted.
hardening_notes: Anonymous traffic evicts tenant request-log rows. The prune is a global newest-N cap (service.py:86-92; config.py:81; docs/configuration.md:88 'approximate cap'). Local check C_F: three anonymous writes at retention 3 removed the tenant's request_log row while its usage_rollups row survived. The usage resource reads request_logs (operations/service.py:101-103), so tenant-visible history shrinks under anonymous traffic. No per-tenant retention is promised, so this is hardening; per-scope retention would be needed if per-tenant usage history is promised.

Synchronous commit on the event loop: security_headers is async (main.py:168) and calls the blocking record_request (main.py:214; service.py:25-43) for every non-health request, including unauthenticated 404s. database.py:19-27 sets no pool size or timeout. Not validated because stress testing is excluded. Owner check: event-loop lag and DB pool saturation under normal load.

Duplicate client X-Request-ID: request_logs.request_id is unique (models.py:35), the client header is used unvalidated (main.py:169), and a duplicate raises IntegrityError that is swallowed (main.py:225-226). Source-derived only; the local check did not exercise a duplicate (driver header-case bug). Impact is limited to the requester's own metadata. Hardening: generate server-side request IDs.
The access log writes raw request.url.path for unmatched routes (main.py:204). json.dumps escapes control characters, so no log injection was found in source.

The same raw route feeds Prometheus observe_http labels (main.py:182-188; packages/relaypay/observability/metrics.py:125-136). That sink is peer-owned and not assessed here; the same route-fallback fix applies to it.

A signature keyed by a random issued-style credential is REJECTED INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE 401. A signature keyed by COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET (the value the route passes, inbound.py:30) PASSES the gate and reaches persistence (dummy factory). A non-ASCII signature raises TypeError before any acceptance (fails closed, no 401 mapping). The DB-backed connector and version state was not exercised.

local_checks.invariant: Activation and revocation of a connector credential version must change what the connector can authenticate, and any documented credential comparison must have an active consumer.
local_checks.result: activate_connector_version (service.py:254-266) sets the prior ACTIVE version to REVOKED and the new version to ACTIVE, and writes nothing else that affects authentication. Connector.status is set to ACTIVE only at insert (service.py:93). Admission reads only connector.status == ACTIVE (service.py:347-354). No code path writes connector status to DISABLED (grep over connectors and admin routes). ConnectorVersion.status and secret_sha256 have no admission reader; ConnectorCredentialVersion is decrypted only in tests (test_m5_connectors.py:158). The rotation test asserts version statuses and decryption only (test_m5_connectors.py:80-170). docs/threat-model.md:23 lists digest-only comparison and rotation as mitigations; docs/configuration.md:70 documents COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET as the HMAC key for inbound connector events. adapters.py:53-65 accepts an unsigned 200 for /health/live and /health/connector during verification, and the probe target comes from settings, not the stored base_url.

local_checks.invariant: Deployed configuration must keep the connector credential key and the commerce control secret scoped to the workloads that need them, and production must refuse dev or placeholder values.
local_checks.result: compose.production.yaml sets APP_ENV production (line 2) and requires CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY and COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET by required substitution (lines 31-32). Dev compose uses dev defaults (compose.yaml:33-34). The shared production anchor (lines 1-33) is applied to ten services (lines 54-80), including commerce, dispute-network, merchant-site and poller, so those workloads also receive CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY and RELAYPAY_DATABASE_URL (line 4). That distribution belongs to a peer-owned compose unit and is referenced, not claimed here. .env.production.example:29 uses a placeholder for the connector key that validation does not reject. The commerce authenticate path compares X-Commerce-Control with hmac.compare_digest against COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET (apps/commerce/main.py:59-62).

local_checks.invariant: Reported security outcome must follow the current source boundary and evidence
local_checks.result: Inbound events signed with the shared commerce control secret can be admitted for an active connector regardless of connector version status. The issued version credential is not the documented inbound signing key, so source does not establish that its holder possesses the shared key or that revocation is intended to cut off inbound access.

local_checks.invariant: Reported security outcome must follow the current source boundary and evidence
local_checks.result: The database-backed admission blocker is locally answerable from the admission and rotation paths. The unresolved question is whether revocation is intended to withdraw a sender's authority to use the shared inbound key.

unresolved: Owner decision: whether version REVOKED status or a connector-level DISABLED state is meant to block inbound events; docs/threat-model.md:23 presents rotation as a mitigation, but no source path reads version status for admission.
DB-backed admission after revocation was not executed; the sandbox has no PostgreSQL fixture, so the local check covers only the signature gate and the dummy persistence boundary.
Compose rendering was not executed; the overlay matrix comes from source reading only.
Inbound key scope (one deployment-wide COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET) and shared production anchor distribution belong to peer-owned units and are referenced, not claimed.
discovery_reason: post_connector_version stores AES-GCM ciphertext of a generated credential (service.py:116, 139) under a key derived as unsalted SHA-256 of CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY (crypto.py:8, 11-13; admin.py:1081), records secret_sha256 as unsalted SHA-256 of the plaintext (service.py:140), hard-codes key_version 1 (service.py:141), and returns the plaintext once (admin.py:1088). decrypt_credential (crypto.py:16-19) has no caller in apps, packages or scripts, and the inbound connector route authenticates events with COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET (inbound.py:30) rather than the issued credential. Units 13-16 review this admin path for business logic, chaining, resource and metadata classes only; the Cryptography class is primary solely for inbound verification in unit 46. Development defaults for both secrets are at config.py:61 and config.py:104.
hardening_notes: Credential generation is server-side only: ConnectorVersionCreate is extra=forbid with no credential field (admin.py:220-221), the token is 256-bit (service.py:116), and each encryption uses a fresh os.urandom(12) nonce (crypto.py:12).
Crypto failure is fail-closed: encryption runs inside session.begin() (admin.py:1071-1083), so an exception rolls back connector and version rows and returns no plaintext.

Plaintext exposure is limited to the single 201 response: no request or response body persistence (observability/service.py:44-54), audit details exclude the secret (service.py:144-152), and API responses carry no-store (apps/api/main.py:176).

Local check C1: the production validator (config.py:96-110) rejects only the dev default. It accepts the documented placeholder GENERATE_A_LONG_RANDOM_VALUE and a one-character key. Because key derivation is a single unsalted SHA-256 (crypto.py:7-8), a weak operator value would be offline-guessable from ciphertext. The consequence is latent because no production path decrypts connector credentials. The peer-owned config.py production-validation unit may already cover this, so it is not claimed as a finding here.

Local check C4: credential ciphertext has no associated data (crypto.py:13,19), so a ciphertext moved to another version row still decrypts. Bind organisation, environment, connector version and credential name as AAD when a decrypt consumer is added. Tampering is rejected.

Documented control is absent: docs/threat-model.md:23 lists digest-only comparison for connector credentials, but secret_sha256 (service.py:140, models.py:95) is written and never read. Either implement a verifier or remove the claim.

validate() (adapters.py:53-65) accepts an unsigned 200 from /health/live or /health/connector. Verification strength therefore depends on the configured probe target. The stored base_url (service.py:125) is unused, and admin verification uses settings URLs (admin.py:1103-1114). No lower-trust input reaches the probe, so this is hardening only.
Rotation test gap: test_m5_connectors.py:80-170 checks statuses and decryption but not that a revoked version stops admitting events, which is why the candidate lifecycle gap is not caught.
key_version is hard-coded to 1 (models.py:96, service.py:142) with no rotation or re-encryption reader. That is architecture, not a vulnerability.

Local check C6: a non-ASCII signature header raises TypeError from hmac.compare_digest on the inbound path. Nothing is accepted, so it fails closed, but the response is an unhandled error rather than 401. The inbound unit is peer-owned; noted for completeness.

local_checks.invariant: Settlement requires organisation-admin authority and cannot reuse an idempotency key to settle a different merchant or repeat a completed effect.
local_checks.result: admin.py:562-590 verifies CSRF and fingerprints the method, route, both path selectors and parsed body. _run_settlement_transaction requires a SESSION with ORGANISATION_ADMIN membership, resolves the scoped environment and locks the scoped merchant. Existing keys are organisation/environment scoped, reject changed fingerprints and return stored response bytes. SettlementRun has a matching unique key constraint. run_settlement wraps the entire operation in session.begin(); its IntegrityError retry starts a fresh transaction after rollback.

local_checks.invariant: Settlement moves each eligible capture's remaining pending payable once, offsets receivables consistently, and commits accounting evidence atomically.
local_checks.result: The settlement query accepts only scoped SUCCEEDED captures belonging to the locked merchant and lacking a SettlementItem. It locks captures and subtracts actual prior REFUND pending deltas from capture.net_amount. Nonpositive results are skipped. Each positive amount debits pending and credits receivable plus available by exactly the same amount; the running receivable offset cannot exceed its initial nonnegative balance. post_refund_journal takes the same merchant lock before reading settlement items and sourcing refunds, while payout creation/retry also lock the merchant. Capture finalization commits its success and journal together. Settlement items, journals, balance transactions, completion bytes and audit are written in the settlement transaction; capture/item and journal uniqueness provide duplicate-effect backstops. Locked captures skipped by SKIP LOCKED remain eligible for a later command. No source-grounded corruption candidate survived this trace; no target code was executed.

discovery_reason: apps/api/routes/admin.py:562-590 invokes a financial mutation distinct from model-based settlement intelligence and payout reservation. merchant_balances/service.py:356-399 performs authority, idempotency and merchant locking; :400-427 selects unsettled captures and refund adjustments; :469-518 writes journals, balance transactions, settlement items and the replay response; :552-561 retries after an integrity error. No current unit reviews this service or these settlement invariants. Trace concurrent settlement/refund interactions, replay conflicts and atomic conservation across failure and retry.

The configured source is a service URL, not a request parameter; the supplied Compose configurations point to the synthetic merchant-site service, whose code returns immutable fixtures and computes their digest. Snapshot reuse includes organisation, environment, site reference and digest, with a matching uniqueness constraint. The HTTP response's digest and site reference are not independently bound to its content or request, but source does not establish a lower-trust actor able to alter that response or the configured source. No security consequence across an established boundary follows from the fixture contract alone.

local_checks.result: The service looks up the scoped snapshot and review before inserting, and database uniqueness constraints prevent duplicate committed rows. discovery_reason: The existing deterministic-checks unit records the claimed-digest behavior as hardening, but does not own the snapshot transport and content-binding boundary. snapshot.py:13-19 validates the supplied digest's shape, and snapshot.py:45-69 accepts the HTTP response as a SiteSnapshot. service.py:73-83 uses that supplied digest to reuse a stored snapshot, while service.py:89-91 stores the supplied content and digest. Review this separate boundary against the synthetic fixture contract and the configured source before deciding whether any lower-trust producer or security consequence is established; apps/merchant_site/main.py:1-6 describes immutable synthetic fixtures, so an external attacker must not be presumed.

local_checks.invariant: Only authenticated, fresh connector events should enter the worker queue, with effective admission bounds considered before alleging starvation.
local_checks.result: The route requires a timestamp and COMMERCE_CONTROL_SECRET-backed HMAC; acceptance also requires an ACTIVE connector. Optional origin authentication guards this path. Database uniqueness limits duplicate connector/event-ID pairs. Neither the direct route nor supplied Caddy configuration establishes an aggregate queue quota. The optional edge adds body and admission controls, but its deployment and effective aggregate limits are not established. No merchant-key or ordinary operator-session path to the signing secret was established.

local_checks.invariant: A failed or concurrently claimed event must not repeatedly occupy the queue head or retain the claim transaction throughout handler execution.
local_checks.result: Claims select one eligible row using SKIP LOCKED, commit a 30-second lease, and release the claim transaction before invoking the commerce handler. Completion is fenced by lease token and PROCESSING status. Handler exceptions become delayed retries, with default dead-lettering after three completed failed attempts. Delayed and terminal rows are excluded from immediate claims. The commerce handler is synchronous and takes a separate payment-link row lock; the lease is not a handler deadline. No single poison-record infinite retry was established.

local_checks.invariant: Inbound work must yield shared scheduler execution to unrelated due safety and delivery tasks.
local_checks.result: _process_inbound_webhooks drains until no eligible claim remains, without a count cap, snapshot cutoff, or time budget. poll_once invokes it synchronously before authorization expiry, PSP application, and outbox publication. The two-second cadence is advanced only after return; exception isolation and the metrics decorator provide no preemption. Compose defines one poller service. Actual worker replication and ingress throughput remain external facts.

local_checks.invariant: New arrivals during an inbound batch must not extend that batch ahead of unrelated due tasks indefinitely.
local_checks.result: The coordinator executed AST-extracted, otherwise unchanged scheduler functions with decorators removed and database, handler, publisher, and other runners replaced by finite instrumented fixtures. One initial claim processed once; four initial claims plus two arrivals processed all six before expiry, PSP application, or publication. Exit code was zero. This proves task ordering and inclusion of new arrivals, not sustained starvation or attacker admission. Execution used the coordinator's network-disabled, read-only sandbox with the prescribed resource limits and dummy data.

local_checks.invariant: Reported security outcome must follow the current source boundary and evidence
local_checks.result: The inbound endpoint can add eligible events to a queue that the synchronous poller drains before running later scheduled tasks. The drain has no batch-start cutoff, claim count limit, or deadline, so arrivals during a drain can extend it. Source does not establish that a lower-trust sender can sustain accepted work long enough to cause meaningful shared delay, or that deployed admission and worker topology permit that effect.

Connector acceptance persists independently selectable event IDs as PENDING work at packages/relaypay/connectors/service.py:353-381; claims select globally rather than by tenant at :404-434. Each claim synchronously reaches commerce synchronization, including a blocking row lock at packages/relaypay/mock_commerce/service.py:94-100. Existing tests specify private permissions, overwrite refusal and symlink refusal; tests were read, not executed.

local_checks.invariant: Credential propagation into the workload must avoid command arguments and retained reports, with execution destinations controlled by the invoking operator.
local_checks.result: run_loadtest.py:39-74 places credentials in TemporaryDirectory, excludes apiKey from tenant.json, and invokes a fixed subprocess argument list without a shell. Script names are restricted by argparse choices; duration is passed as an environment value. compose.load.yaml:6-17 forwards selected workload variables and mounts the credential file read-only, rather than placing the key in environment or argv. common.js:30-48 uses the key only in the Authorization header; its summary at :79-96 retains aggregates and workload metadata. All five entry scripts delegate to this common path. machine_info.py:46-96 returns selected host/database metadata, not credentials. LOAD_BASE_URL is operator-controlled and defaults to the local API; no lower-trust destination setter was established. Temporary-directory cleanup surrounds subprocess failure as well as normal completion. No target execution occurred.

hardening_notes: Load keys remain ACTIVE after temporary-file removal, as explicitly documented in loadtest/README.md. Consider revoking the generated key in runner cleanup, including subprocess startup failures; current source establishes only a fresh scoped TEST tenant, not a cross-principal compromise.

The standalone seed CLI permits arbitrary operator-selected output paths. Document keeping those files outside image COPY roots and package inputs; the normal runner already uses a separate temporary directory.

local_checks.invariant: Generated load credentials must not enter retained load artifacts or become an image build input through the normal runner.
local_checks.result: run_loadtest.py:29-45 writes retained artifacts beneath output/load but creates the plaintext credential file in a separate TemporaryDirectory. machine_info.py:76-96 constructs an explicit metadata result. compose.load.yaml uses a prebuilt k6 image and a runtime read-only credential bind mount; run_loadtest.py:59-73 runs it with --rm and --no-deps without invoking a build. loadtest_seed.py accepts an operator-selected standalone output path, but no automatic build handoff from that path or lower-trust actor controlling it was established.

local_checks.invariant: Repository build and package inputs must not capture the credential files or retained output produced by the load runner.
local_checks.result: compose.yaml:108-110 and :129-131 use the repository root as Python image context. .dockerignore:13 excludes output, and .gitignore excludes output from normal tracking. Dockerfile.python copies selected manifests, packages, apps, migrations and scripts; it does not copy the repository root or load output wholesale. Dockerfile.console copies console inputs and built output. pyproject.toml:49-50 restricts wheel packages to relaypay and relaypay_sdk. The normal credential file is outside these inputs. No source-grounded handoff of a real load credential into a resulting image or wheel was found; image builds were not executed.
